## Facility environmental compliance specialist — federal variant (P4)

*Function:* Keep a regulated facility in documented compliance with its permits, rules and reporting obligations.

*X4 match:* `skos:relatedMatch` (confidence 0.35, applies to: combined safety duties; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulated-party.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-5 to GS-7 (entry); GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- **Manage a regulated facility's environmental compliance system and obligations calendar** — 55%
  - Develop a facility compliance checklist and procedures from its permits and applicable rules, assigning an owner and deadline to each obligation *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Prepare a periodic compliance report for the facility, checking reported values against source data before the responsible official certifies it *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Update the facility compliance calendar when a permit, rule or reporting requirement changes, notifying each obligation owner of the change *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Investigate a permit exceedance at the facility, identifying the root cause and documenting corrective actions and the notice given to the agency *(critical)*
- **Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance** — 10%
  - Screen automated regulatory-change alerts for a program each week, confirming which items affect its decisions and recording why the rest do not *(needed at entry)*
  - Update program procedures and templates to a new governing version, recording which pending actions follow the old and new versions
- **Manage field sample custody and field quality control** — 10%
  - Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them *(needed at entry)*
- **Manage regulated-entity disclosure and compliance across divergent regimes** — 5%
  - Prepare a mandatory disclosure report from controlled data collected across operations, tracing each reported figure to its source system
- **Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites** — 5%
  - Follow a site health and safety plan at a contaminated or industrial site, observing zone boundaries, air-monitoring action levels and decontamination steps *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Identify signs of potential hazardous materials at a field site, such as drums, stained soil, odours or unusual debris, before disturbing them *(critical, needed at entry)*
- **Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings** — 4%
  - Deliver a pre-work safety briefing that covers site hazards, controls, communications and the stop-work procedure for the assigned work area
  - Exercise stop-work authority when field, facility or incident conditions exceed the stated safety limits of the assignment *(critical, needed at entry)*
- **Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary** — 3%
  - Apply post-employment restrictions when moving between a regulator and a regulated party, obtaining written ethics advice before contact on covered matters *(critical)*
  - Disclose financial, employment or relationship interests that could affect an assignment before work begins, using the organization's conflict form *(needed at entry)*
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record** — 2%
  - Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance
- **Build organizational and jurisdictional greenhouse gas inventories for disclosure and reporting** — 2%
  - Compile a greenhouse gas inventory for an organization or jurisdiction, documenting boundaries, activity data, emission factors and methods for each source.
- **Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action** — 2%
  - Track the status of each authorization for a project against the pathway plan, notifying the project team when a delay moves the critical path
- **Record provenance and AI involvement in work products** — 2%
  - Record the source, date, version, method and any AI tool used for a dataset or analysis, using the organization's provenance template. *(needed at entry)*

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: manage a regulated facility's environmental compliance system and obligations calendar (EMST target entry L1, journey L2). *Distinguishing.*
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage field sample custody and field quality control (EMST target entry L1, journey L2).
- Knowledge of and skill in: maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary (EMST target entry L1, journey L2).
- Knowledge of and skill in: track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance (EMST target entry L1, journey L2).
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage regulated-entity disclosure and compliance across divergent regimes (EMST target entry L1, journey L2).
- Knowledge of and skill in: apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings (EMST target entry L1, journey L2).
  - A no-blame incident review separates system and condition causes from individual error and sanctions only reckless or wilful acts, so that people keep reporting near misses.
  - Stop-work authority lets any worker halt a task they judge unsafe; the task resumes only after the hazard is assessed and the plan revised, and the person who stopped it is not penalized.
- Knowledge of and skill in: work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites (EMST target entry L1, journey L2).
